Subject: Lumen Health — post-demo TCO & deployment-mode follow-ups

Hi Sam — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our call (keeps it actionable):

What we heard
- Primary use case: triage + summarization for patient intake forms (latency target sub-300ms p99 for 512-token responses).
- Volume: initial pilot ~1M user-visible tokens/month, expected growth to 5–10M over 12 months.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in prompts; Lumen prefers VPC or on-prem control for production.

High-level deployment options we recommend (short):
1) Hosted API — fastest to ship (no infra ops), per-token pricing. Good for early pilot if PHI can be routed through our private tenancy + strict retention rules.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — predictable latency and lower unit cost at scale; commit for capacity (monthly/annual) with burst headroom.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — full network control and KMS integration for PHI, higher setup time but needed for long-term regulated deployment.

Attached: a quick spreadsheet with two scenarios (1M tokens/mo pilot and a 5M tokens/mo steady state) that compares per-token hosted pricing vs 3-tier dedicated commit options. Also attached a one-pager pricing summary.

Ask / next steps
- Can you confirm pilot constraints (allowed hosting modes for pilot: hosted API with VPC tenancy vs dedicated in customer VPC vs on-prem)?
- Which scenario should we model as the baseline for the commercial playbook (1M tokens/mo pilot is our default unless you ask otherwise).
- I recommend a short follow-up next week to walk the spreadsheet assumptions and required security artifacts for a VPC/private deployment.

If it helps, we can do a 30-minute math session where we align on token definitions, expected concurrency, and retention — then Karthik can produce a recommended commit ask and discount grid.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications so we model correctly:

1) Pilot hosting: our security team is open to a dedicated VPC instance (customer-managed VPC peering) for pilot if we can get KMS integration + SOC2 evidence. Hosted multi-tenant API is only acceptable if data never leaves our VPC via egress — can you confirm tenancy options?

2) Cost ask: please include a line for a 6-month reserved commit for Dedicated (assume 8x high-memory A100-class GPUs) and a hosted per-token cost for 1M tokens/mo and 5M tokens/mo. We also want a row showing amortized egress/storage for logs and KV cache (likely 500GB/month).

3) SLA: can you include a target latency SLO note (p95/p99) for each deployment mode? p99 < 300ms is a hard requirement for the UI flow.

We'll loop security next. Can you share the spreadsheet before EOD PST so our procurement can start modeling?

Sam — thanks, appreciate the clear asks. I attached a revised workbook with the 6-month reserved commit rows and a dedicated VPC sketch (assumptions tab). Highlights:

- Hosted (per-token): modeled using our standard V2 rate with PHI retention controls — pilot (1M tokens/mo) = $0.0009/token effective; 5M tokens/mo shows marginal volume pricing to $0.0007/token in our example. (See sheet: hosted_pricing)
- Dedicated (reserved): modeled 8x A100-equivalent nodes; blended monthly cost in sheet results in an effective token cost of ~$0.00045/token at 5M tokens/mo (this assumes 60% GPU utilization and SmartBatch reduces per-token GPU time by ~22%).
- Private VPC / on-prem: one-time setup + ongoing infra ops modeled; unit cost nearer to dedicated at scale but higher TCO in first 6 months.
- Storage / egress: we added a separate line for 500GB/month at $0.03/GB (logs + KV snapshots).
- SLAs: Hosted: p95 < 120ms, p99 ~ 350ms (depends on region/sequence length); Dedicated: p95 < 80ms, p99 < 220ms (with pinned capacity); Private: comparable to dedicated after tuning. We flagged p99 for hosted as a risk for sub-300ms requirement — dedicated or private is recommended for the UI path.

I've included the assumptions tab in Lumen_1M_token_model.xlsx — please confirm tokens definition (are we counting user-visible tokens only, or including system & tool tokens?). Once you confirm, Karthik will produce a recommended commit band and discount matrix for the procurement packet.

If you want, we can run a 2-week canary on dedicated infra (no long-term commit) to validate latency and utilization before a 6-month reserved ask. That typically removes the risk for procurement.

Best — Jordan
